text:
Sam: heads up — after `brew install redwoodctl` on an M1 mac, `redwoodctl login` finishes in the browser but `redwoodctl whoami` returns "no active session".
Priya: are you using the system Node or brew node?
Sam: system node (preinstalled). Also noticed config ended up at ~/.config/redwood/settings.json while local dev tools are reading ~/.redwood/config.json.
Theo: that mismatch rings a bell. We moved to XDG paths in the last minor release but left the local-serve code pointing at the legacy dotdir.
Sam: workaround was copying the file `cp ~/.config/redwood/settings.json ~/.redwood/config.json` and then `whoami` showed my user. But install-completion also failed: postinstall tries to append to ~/.bashrc and errors on zsh.
Priya: sigh, shell detection logic in postinstall is brittle. For now you can run `redwoodctl install-completion --shell=zsh` which writes to ~/.config/zsh/completions.
Theo: immediate steps: 1) make CLI prefer XDG paths first, legacy dotfiles second; 2) add a migration step on first run that moves legacy state into XDG if present; 3) patch postinstall to detect fish/zsh/bash robustly and not throw.
Sam: also saw auth retries hammer the provider during a transient outage. retry jitter is too small and we spike 429s in CI.
QA Bot: please include a reproducible test case and CI job for `redwoodctl login` so we catch this in PRs.
Theo: will add an e2e against the test auth client and bump backoff/jitter values.
DevEx Bot: Created RW-2410: "unify config paths, add migration, robust shell completion install, and auth retry tuning" assigned to Theo, priority P2. Link: https://issues.internal/RW-2410
Ops: also double-check our package maintainers publish scripts — conflict between npm and homebrew installers could be causing different default paths.
Sam: thanks, copying the files fixed me for now. Marking resolved on my side. :thumbsup:
